message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you set). Points come from opponents’ remaining cards when someone goes “Out.” | | **Setup** | Shuffle a standard Uno deck (108 cards). Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the rest face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Actions** | 1️⃣ Play one card that matches either color or number/symbol of the top discard.
2️⃣ If you have no match, draw one card. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately. | | **Special Cards** | • **+2** – Next player draws two and skips.
• **Reverse** – Changes direction of play.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **+4 Wild** – Choose color + next player draws four (must be used only if you truly have no matching color). | | **Going Out** | When you play your last card, shout “Uno!” before your opponent’s turn starts. If you forget, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Scoring** | After a round ends, add up the point values of all cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value
• +2, Reverse, Skip = 20 pts
• Wild, +4 Wild = 50 pts | | **Winning** | First to reach 500 points wins the game (you can adjust this target). | **Key Tips** * Keep track of what colors are being played—if you’re low on a certain color, try to force others to draw with +2 or +4. * Use Wild cards strategically to change the color to something you have many of. * Remember the “Uno” rule: if you’re caught not saying it, you’ll pay a penalty. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak house rules (e.g., “Draw 3” instead of “+2”) to keep things fresh.
